Carne Cruda All'albese

Fresh Piedmont Fassona beef finely chopped by hand and dressed with extra-virgin olive oil, salt, pepper, and optional lemon and white truffle.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/8 lb very fresh lean Fassona beef, such as top round, eye round, or tenderloin
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
juice of 1/2 lemon, optional
1 garlic clove, optional
about 3 tbsp thinly shaved Alba white truffle, optional

Preparation

1. Keep the beef, knife, and cutting board very cold until ready to prepare.

2. Remove all fat, membrane, and connective tissue from the beef.

3. Cut first into thin slices.

4. Cut the slices into narrow strips.

5. Chop finely by hand until tender but not paste-like.

6. For a subtle garlic aroma, rub the garlic clove around the serving bowl and discard it.

7. Put the beef in the bowl.

8. Add the olive oil, salt, and pepper.

9. Toss gently.

10. Add the lemon only if desired and immediately before serving.

Service

Shape portions without compacting the meat and, in season, finish with thin white-truffle shavings.

Chef's note

Keep the beef cold and season only at the last moment, especially when using lemon.

Bagna Càuda

Warm Piedmont garlic-and-anchovy dip served in individual warmers with raw and cooked vegetables.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 heads garlic, about 40 cloves
10 salt-packed anchovies
2 cups plus 2 tbsp olive oil
1 1/2 tbsp butter
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk, optional for mellowing the garlic

For serving
4 roasted bell peppers
4 cardoons or cardoon ribs
4 small heads radicchio
4 boiled potatoes
4 cooked onions

Preparation

1. Separate the garlic heads into cloves.

2. Peel the cloves and remove the inner germ.

3. For a milder version, put the garlic in a saucepan with the milk.

4. Cook slowly until a fork passes easily through the cloves.

5. Drain and discard the milk.

6. Finely chop the garlic.

7. Desalt and debone the anchovies thoroughly.

8. Put the garlic in a saucepan with about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon olive oil.

9. Add the anchovies.

10. Cook over the lowest possible heat without ever letting the oil boil.

11. Stir continuously for about 10 minutes, until the garlic and anchovies form a uniform mixture.

12. Gradually add the remaining olive oil.

13. Remove from the heat.

14. Stir in the butter.

Service

Transfer to individual warmers and keep hot without frying. Dip the vegetables directly into the sauce.

Chef's note

Bagna càuda should stay hot but never fry. Excessive heat makes both garlic and anchovies bitter.

Roasted Peppers with Anchovies

1. Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes after the water reaches a boil.

2. Cool, peel, and separate the yolks.

3. Desalt the anchovies thoroughly under cold water.

4. Open them flat and remove the backbone and pin bones.

7. Finely chop the garlic, parsley, and hard-boiled yolks.

8. Transfer to a bowl.

9. Add the olive oil, vinegar, chile, and salt.

11. Cover the anchovies completely with the sauce.

12. Cover the platter.

13. Refrigerate for 6–7 hours.

Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes and serve with bread.

Chef's note

The long rest softens the anchovies' saltiness and lets the green sauce season them completely.

Piedmont Russian Salad

Piedmont potato, carrot, pea, tuna, and homemade-mayonnaise salad.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 2 1/3 cups diced potatoes
1 cup diced carrots
1 1/3 cups peas
2 large eggs for garnish
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp white-wine vinegar
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the mayonnaise
2 egg yolks
about 3/4 cup drained oil-packed tuna
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp sunflower oil
juice of 1/2 lemon
1 tsp mustard
1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Peel the potatoes and carrots.

2. Cut into 3/16-inch cubes.

3. Boil the potatoes separately in salted water for 6–8 minutes.

4. Boil the carrots separately for 6–8 minutes.

5. Boil the peas for 5 minutes.

6. Immediately chill the peas in ice water.

7. Drain all of the vegetables on a clean kitchen towel.

8. While still warm, dress with the extra-virgin olive oil, vinegar, and salt.

9. Hard-boil the 2 garnish eggs for 8–9 minutes.

10. Cool, peel, and cut into wedges.

11. For the mayonnaise, put the yolks in a bowl with the salt, pepper, and lemon juice.

12. Beat with an electric whisk.

13. Gradually stream in the sunflower oil while whisking continuously.

14. Add the mustard.

15. Finely chop the tuna.

16. Fold it into the mayonnaise.

17. Add the mayonnaise to the vegetables.

18. Mix gently.

19. Cover.

20. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours.

Service

Garnish with the hard-boiled egg wedges and serve cold.

Chef's note

Cutting all of the vegetables to the same size creates an even texture and prevents some pieces from becoming soft before others.

Thinning the central rib makes the cabbage leaves flexible enough to close without tearing.

Fassona Albese

Paper-thin Piedmont Fassona beef with Parmigiano cream, arugula cream, and dried tomato powder.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb Fassona eye round, completely trimmed
3 1/3 cups Piccadilly or plum tomatoes
about 5 cups finely grated 36-month Parmigiano Reggiano
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp heavy cream
about 20 cups loosely packed arugula
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Trim the eye round completely of fat and connective tissue.

2. Wrap tightly in plastic and then foil.

3. Freeze at very low temperature until completely firm.

4. Preheat the oven to 320°F.

5. Cut the tomatoes in half.

6. Arrange on a baking sheet.

7. Bake for 20 minutes.

8. Drain the released liquid.

9. Dry the tomatoes at about 130°F for roughly 12 hours, until completely dry.

10. Grind into a powder.

11. Add about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

12. Blend the arugula with 3/4 cup olive oil until smooth.

13. Add about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

14. Bring the cream almost to a boil.

15. Remove from the heat.

16. Gradually add the grated Parmigiano.

17. Stir until smooth.

18. Cool.

19. Slice the still-firm beef paper-thin on a slicer.

20. Arrange on plates.

21. Let the meat temper for 3–5 minutes.

Service

Finish the Fassona with small amounts of Parmigiano cream, arugula cream, tomato powder, and the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

The beef must remain very cold and firm to produce extremely thin, even slices on the slicer.

Keeping some of the bean liquid creates a creamy sauce without cream or other thickeners.

Tuscan Cecina

Thin Tuscan chickpea flatbread made with chickpea flour, water, extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

3 1/3 cups chickpea flour
4 1/4 cups water
1/4 cup plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 2 tbsp for the pan
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the chickpea flour in a large bowl.

2. Gradually whisk in the water until the batter is smooth and very thin.

3. Add the salt.

4. Cover and rest for at least 4 hours.

5. During resting, skim away any foam that rises to the surface.

6. Add the olive oil and whisk vigorously.

7. Preheat the oven as hot as possible, at least 480°F.

8. Coat a wide shallow pan generously with the remaining olive oil.

9. Pour in the batter in a thin layer.

10. Bake until deeply golden and beginning to char lightly, about 12–18 minutes.

11. Finish with black pepper.

Service

Cut into pieces and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Cecina should be very thin. A wide pan promotes a crisp crust and prevents the center from staying overly soft.
